subject: governance
title: You are not a king on Venus
one_line: Automatic means your discretion was spent once, at writing time, and is now gone.

sections.heading: A king decides each case
body: That is the definition, not an insult. A king's authority is that the case comes to him and he rules on it, and the ruling is authoritative because of who made it. Every case is a fresh opportunity to decide differently, which is the same thing as saying no case is settled by the last one.
Everything anybody dislikes about arbitrary power follows from that single property. Not cruelty, not greed — just the fact that the decision is available to be made again.

sections.heading: A president executes a rule
body: The office is bounded three ways: by a rule written before the case arrived, by a term that ends, and by somebody who can overrule. Take away any of the three and you have a king with better paperwork.

The interesting one is the first. A president who writes the rule and then applies it to a case in front of them has collapsed the two roles, and the collapse is invisible from outside because the output looks the same either way — a decision, in an office, with a reason attached.

sections.heading: Automatic is not a convenience
body: Here is the whole point. When you automate something, your discretion is spent ONCE, at the moment you write the rule, and afterwards it is gone. You cannot make an exception for this case because the code does not know this case is different, and the reason it does not know is that you did not tell it, and the reason you did not tell it is that you did not know either.

People describe automation as a labour saving. It is a constitutional change. The relay in this yard gets one start button and one shutdown, and nothing in between, because anything in between would be a king reaching into a running process.

So a rule that consults the clock, or a random source, or any state you can reach in and change, is not automatic. It is a discretion with a delay on it, and the check below finds exactly that by reading your own source.

sections.heading: More than a few judges
body: One reviewer is a king with extra steps. Two deadlock. The reason benches are odd-numbered and larger than three is that you want a majority that no single member can produce and no single member can block.

The product of a bench is not the ruling. Any one judge could have produced a ruling. The product is the ruling together with the dissent, because the dissent is the record that the other reading existed and lost, which is the only thing that makes a later court able to change its mind honestly.
This is why the drafters in this yard sign their opinions. An unsigned dissent is not a dissent, it is a rumour.

sections.heading: What it costs
body: Slower, and sometimes wrong in a way a king would not have been. A bench cannot fix the case in front of it if fixing it requires ignoring the rule, and there will be cases where that is obviously the right thing to do and it will not be done.

That is the trade being made and it should be made with open eyes. You are buying the property that the next case gets the same treatment as this one, and you are paying for it with the cases where the same treatment is the wrong treatment.

practice.brief: Write apply(rule, cases) so it is genuinely automatic, and panel(votes) so it is genuinely a bench. The checks verify the behaviour and then read your own source to prove apply consults nothing outside its arguments. Then type check.

checks.name: the rule keeps what it should
the same cases in a different order give the same answer
it does not mutate what it was handed
checks.test: (() => { const c = [1,3,2,4]; apply(n => n > 2, c); return JSON.stringify(c) === '[1,3,2,4]'; })()

checks.name: running it twice gives the same answer
it never reads a clock or a random source
a bench of five ruling three to two says so, dissent included
the minority is recorded even when it loses badly
an even split is a deadlock, not a ruling
one judge cannot rule alone on a bench of five
no judge is named anywhere in it

ask: Find the place in your own work where you kept a discretion. Say why you kept it, or spend it.
